title: EUDR reference-number desk for downstream buyers
one_liner: An inbox-and-validator service that collects, checks and vaults EUDR reference numbers and plot GeoJSON from suppliers, sold to downstream operators and via customs brokers.
customer: Mid-size EU importers, traders and manufacturers who buy EUDR goods (wood and furniture components, coffee, cocoa, leather, rubber parts, palm derivatives) after a first operator has placed them on the market. The second channel is customs brokers and freight forwarders who white-label the desk.
problem: From 30 Dec 2026, large and medium operators and traders must comply. Downstream operators no longer file due diligence statements but must collect and keep upstream reference and verification numbers for 5 years. They cannot place goods on the market if the numbers are missing when evidently required. One guide estimates 15-30 minutes per supplier per plot for chasing, format fixes and plausibility checks, which is 'several person-weeks' at 150 suppliers, every year. Typical data faults are self-intersecting polygons from phone apps, areas off by 100x, national coordinate systems instead of WGS 84, plots outside the declared country and duplicates.
solution: A forward-to inbox and portal that (1) extracts reference and verification numbers and GeoJSON from supplier emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and invoices; (2) runs geometry checks on closed rings, self-intersection, WGS 84 with six decimals, the 4-hectare polygon rule, plot inside the declared country, duplicates and area versus tonnage plausibility; (3) auto-sends the supplier a plain-language fix request in their language, with a mobile-friendly plot-drawing link; (4) keeps a 5-year evidence vault; and (5) shows a per-purchase-order 'safe to ship or resell' status. Ship a free public GeoJSON validator first as the lead magnet.
why_now: The 30 Dec 2026 application date is fixed. The Commission's May 2026 review said the regulation will not be reopened and proposed a wider product scope through a draft delegated act, so more mid-size buyers will be pulled in. The EU TRACES NT system was reported not fully operational for the December 2025 date, so integration surprises remain.
revenue_model: SaaS tiers of EUR 79-249 per month by supplier count, plus EUR 1-3 per consignment checked. White-label to brokers at EUR 0.50-3 per declaration or a flat EUR 500-2,000 per month. Optional paid supplier-data cleanup projects.
non_obvious_insight: Filing software is crowded, but 'no DDS needed' makes downstream buyers feel safe while they inherit the messiest job: chasing numbers by email from dozens of suppliers, with a 5-year retention duty and a day-one commercial gate. As one guide puts it, 'Market access, not the fine, is the mechanism that will change behaviour first', because customers cannot resell goods without the numbers (https://www.omnia-analytics.at/en/blog/eudr-2026-operator-data-requirements, which also gives the 15-30 minute estimate and the polygon error list). Incorrect polygon format is reported as a leading cause of DDS rejection (https://www.coolset.com/academy/eudr-geolocation-requirements-how-to-collect-and-validate-gps-polygon-data-for-your-dds). Manufacturers 'do not consider themselves agricultural commodity buyers' yet inherit the duty (https://www.regilient.ai/blog/eudr-due-diligence-product-traceability-compliance). Fixing data at the supplier gives free viral distribution, because each supplier serves many buyers.
first_30_days: Build the public GeoJSON checker using open geometry libraries and rank it for searches like 'EUDR GeoJSON self-intersection error'. Pitch 3 customs brokers and 3 coffee, timber or furniture importers with a manual concierge version: they forward supplier emails and you return a cleaned register within 48 hours. Charge EUR 500 for a one-off audit of their existing supplier files. Use the audits to find the 10 most common data faults and build fix templates.

title: Step-Down Club: Maintenance After the Max Dose
one_liner: A cheap maintenance membership that turns the majority of GLP-1 users who quit or plateau into a planned step-down and a monetizable restart.
customer: Adults 3-12 months into a cash-pay GLP-1 who have hit goal or are about to quit over cost (consumer pays); telehealths and pharmacies pay a bounty per verified restart.
problem: About one-third of non-diabetic obesity patients are still on therapy at 1 year. Stoppers regain roughly 4x faster than people who lost weight with behavior change, and ~60% of ex-users say they intend to restart. Every company optimizes for staying on the max dose, and nobody sells the middle path or owns the ex-user.
solution: At plateau, a physician-written protocol steps the user down to the lowest effective dose or a planned holiday. A connected scale plus waist and strength check-ins run on SMS. Pre-agreed regain triggers (e.g. +3% above nadir for 2 consecutive weeks) auto-route the user to the cheapest legitimate restart, such as a $149 pill program. Optional 'regain warranty' credit as an add-on.
why_now: SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN (Lancet, 2026) is the first RCT showing a reduced 5 mg tirzepatide dose kept about 70% of the weight loss (-16.6% vs -21.9% at max dose vs -9.9% on placebo). $149-$299 pills (Wegovy pill Jan 2026, Foundayo Apr 2026) make restart cheap. Telehealths are converging on the same price and now compete on acquisition cost.
revenue_model: $19-29/month membership, plus $75-150 partner bounty per verified restart or step-down conversion (a telehealth's first-fill CAC is est. $150-400), plus optional warranty add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Discontinuation is the modal outcome, not a failure mode. A restart is a lead worth more than the membership fee, so whoever owns the ex-user relationship owns the cheapest reacquisition channel in a market where every competitor sells the same drug at the same price.
first_30_days: Recruit 100 plateaued or ex-users from r/Zepbound, r/Semaglutide and Facebook groups. Have an obesity-medicine MD write the step-down and restart protocol. Run the check-ins on SMS with a BYO or $25 scale. Sign one telehealth or pharmacy partner for a per-restart bounty. Charge $19/month from day one.

title: Make Platforms and Receiving Banks Pay Scam Refunds
one_liner: A contingency-fee desk that packages evidence so banks can recover mandatory scam reimbursements from receiving institutions and, in the EU, from the platforms where the scam ran.
customer: UK and EU challenger banks, building societies, credit unions, and e-money and payment institutions. Buyers are fraud-recovery and operations heads.
problem: In the UK, PSPs have had to reimburse authorized push-payment scam victims up to GBP 85K since Oct 2024, with the cost split 50:50 between sending and receiving firms. The EU's provisional PSR deal extends liability to bank-impersonation scams and to platforms that ignore fraud notices. Banks treat reimbursement as a cost of business. Recovering from the other side of the chain (the mule-hosting bank, the ad or profile platform) is manual, slow, and mostly abandoned.
solution: Ingest reimbursed case files and auto-build claim dossiers: a timeline, hash-stamped screenshots of the scam ad or profile, the platform notification and its response time, mule-account indicators, and a funds trace. File claims through scheme channels and formal notices to platforms. Track deadlines and disputes. Get paid a percentage of what is actually recovered.
why_now: Mandatory reimbursement now has more than a year of claim volume in the UK. The EU deal shifts costs toward platforms. Investigations into scam-ad revenue have made platform accountability a political priority. Nobody yet holds the data on which counterparties pay and how fast.
revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered value, with a small SaaS floor. A mid-size UK institution reimbursing GBP 10-30M a year can justify six-figure annual fees.
non_obvious_insight: Liability rules create a claims market. The value chain of counterparties is unbilled because banks were told to reimburse victims, not to chase others, and the recovery data is a compounding moat. Whoever holds it can also sell it to regulators.
first_30_days: Offer 10 UK EMIs and small banks a free audit of 50 reimbursed cases showing recoverable amounts from receiving-side firms and disputed shares. Sign contingency contracts with the first 3. Hire one ex-fraud-ops analyst and use spreadsheets and templates before automating.

title: Used-Satellite Exchange With Independent Health Reports
one_liner: A broker and due-diligence shop that turns dead or distressed operators' on-orbit assets into sellable, verified inventory.
customer: Buyers: acquirers of the Rocket Lab type, infrastructure and PE funds, and governments or startups that want a quick constellation. Sellers: bankruptcy trustees, venture-debt lenders, insurers and cash-strapped first-generation smallsat operators.
problem: Insiders assume a satellite is worthless when its company dies. But the bus, license, orbit and customer contracts can still hold value, and buyers cannot verify condition. Lenders have no repossession or title process, and every M&A team improvises technical diligence.
solution: Two products. (1) An independent 'fleet health report' built from open orbital data (maneuver history, decay, propulsion-use proxies, beacon and telemetry checks) plus data-room review. (2) A brokerage that matches on-orbit assets and licenses to buyers, with regulator-approved license transfers handled by counsel.
why_now: Rocket Lab's roughly $8B Iridium deal and its CFO's 'more M&A' comment show on-orbit assets are being priced. 4,517 satellites deployed in 2025 means a large aging first-generation cohort. Funding is bifurcating into nine-figure rounds for a few winners and starvation for the rest.
revenue_model: $25-100k per health report. 3-8% success fee on brokered deals. Annual subscription for lenders and insurers who want portfolio monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: In space, value sits in the license, the orbit and the operating bus, and none of the three dies with the company. The missing piece is trusted third-party verification, which is a service business rather than a rocket business.
first_30_days: Publish free health scorecards on 20 public constellations to build credibility. Interview five venture-debt lenders and two space insurers about their current diligence. Sell two paid reports to funds looking at consolidation targets. Ask trustees of failed smallsat companies to list assets with you.

title: Overtourism Feed for AI Travel Agents
one_liner: A destination-signed, machine-readable feed of live capacity, closures and dispersal incentives that AI trip agents query, so places can steer planning before tourists arrive.
customer: Destination management organisations and city tourism boards in overtouristed regions (Balearics, Dolomites, Kyoto, Lisbon, Dubrovnik, Amsterdam), later transport agencies and hotel groups.
problem: AI agents now plan and book trips (Booking.com and Expedia apps run inside ChatGPT), and they recommend the same hotspots blind to caps, closures and crowding. DMOs intervene only after arrival with fees and fines, which Venice's reportedly ineffective day-tripper fee shows is weak. Referral traffic from search is being eaten by AI answers.
solution: Publish an MCP server and JSON feed per destination with a daily load index by place and hour (from ticketing, parking, cruise calendars and occupancy), hard caps and permits, equivalent alternatives within about 60 minutes with partner lodging, resident-first hours and off-peak incentive codes. DMOs get a dashboard showing how many agent-planned trips shifted. Start with a hosted API and a DMO-embedded chatbot for immediate use.
why_now: OTA apps are now inside AI assistants, MCP servers are mainstream, booking lead times are shrinking, and AI overviews reportedly cut metasearch clicks by 31% in tested markets. DMOs need a way to influence the plan rather than the queue.
revenue_model: DMO subscriptions of EUR 20-100K per year, transparent sponsored 'dispersal' placements paid by under-visited partners, and analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism control is an information-timing problem. Influence must happen at itinerary generation, and AI agents are the first chokepoint where a single feed can shape millions of itineraries, giving destinations robots.txt-style power.
first_30_days: Build a feed for one region from public data (cruise schedules, park permit status, museum time slots) and ship the MCP server. Offer 3 DMOs a free traffic dashboard as design partners and embed it in their own website chatbots. Approach trip-planner app builders for consumption.

title: Digital Legacy Setup Sold Through Wealth Advisors
one_liner: A white-labeled 'digital safety and legacy' visit for advisors' 80+ clients, paid for by the advisor as a retention and heir-acquisition tool.
customer: Independent RIAs and trust departments with $100M-$2B in assets and many clients over 78, plus elder-law attorneys as a secondary channel.
problem: Industry surveys often find that a majority of heirs fire their parents' advisor after an inheritance. Regulators also expect vigilance on senior clients, with trusted-contact requirements (FINRA 4512) and hold authority (Rule 2165). Meanwhile the 80-year-old's digital life (email, photos, passwords, crypto, cloud accounts, carrier, bank portals) is unmanaged. When they die or lose capacity the family can't get in, and scammers can.
solution: A 90-minute in-home or video visit by a trained 'digital steward': account inventory, password manager and passkey setup, Apple Legacy Contact and Google Inactive Account Manager set up, carrier port-out locks and credit freezes, bank alerts with 2FA routed to a trusted contact, and a family emergency binder handed to the heir or trustee. The heir joins the final visit, introduced by the advisor as the person who organized it. Add an annual re-check.
why_now: The multi-trillion-dollar generational wealth transfer is underway. More wealth sits in crypto and online accounts. Deepfake voice-clone scams target seniors. Apple and Google have shipped legacy-contact features but adoption is low, and FINRA's 2026 oversight report keeps trusted-contact practices in focus.
revenue_model: $450-900 per client visit paid by the advisor, who may pass it through, plus a $150/yr maintenance subscription. Referral fees from elder-law attorneys.
non_obvious_insight: The payer isn't the 80-year-old. It's the advisor, whose most valuable asset, the client relationship, is about to leave with the heirs. A digital steward visit is a useful favor that puts the advisor in the room with the next generation, and it doubles as compliance-friendly protection.
first_30_days: Recruit 5-10 RIAs through one advisor community (XYPN or local FPA chapters) and offer 3 free client visits each in exchange for feedback and a signed pilot. Hire retired IT pros or college students and train them on a checklist. Track how many heirs attend and whether advisors get follow-up meetings.

title: Continuity Assurance for Emotional AI Products
one_liner: A regression-testing and escrow layer that lets companion, coaching and therapy-adjacent apps swap underlying models without users feeling the presence they know has died.
customer: Builders of AI companion, coaching, journaling and tutoring apps with 50k+ users, paying $2-10k a month, plus $15-40k per migration project.
problem: Trend chain: labs retire models every 6-12 months (OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT on 13 Feb 2026 and the #Keep4o backlash followed), then every app on a rented model faces a forced swap, then nobody can measure whether the voice, memory use, warmth and boundaries survived. Drift toward more sycophancy is also a safety risk for vulnerable users.
solution: (1) Extract a 'persona fingerprint' (tone, boundaries, memory behavior) from historical transcripts. (2) A swap-regression suite of 300+ scenarios (comfort, boundary-setting, crisis, sycophancy, memory recall) with human-rater calibration. (3) A portable memory-and-persona bundle users can export. (4) Optional escrow of memory and configuration with a neutral custodian and a shutdown covenant.
why_now: #Keep4o proved model deprecation causes real grief. Deprecation cycles are accelerating across vendors. California SB 243 (effective Jan 2026) raises documentation duties on companion operators, and the Pew data show public distrust that punishes visible harms.
revenue_model: SaaS by monthly active users ($2-10k a month), migration projects ($15-40k), and escrow retainers (about $500 a month).
non_obvious_insight: Users do not mourn a model, they mourn a relationship state (memory plus idiolect) that the app owns and can port. The lab's model is a replaceable engine, and nobody sells the warmth-preserving transmission between engines.
first_30_days: Interview 15 companion and coaching founders. Build a v0 eval on three open-weight model pairs. Offer free 'swap audits' to three apps, then convert the two most nervous ones to paid.

title: Loss Draft Desk for Storm Contractors
one_liner: Software and concierge service that gets contractors and homeowners through the mortgage servicer's loss-draft process, then advances cash against approved draws.
customer: Storm-restoration general contractors, roofers and owner-builders working on mortgage-encumbered repairs and rebuilds, starting with the Palisades and Eaton rebuild wave and Gulf Coast stragglers. Later, homeowners and the servicers' own vendor teams.
problem: The carrier pays, but the money is not free: the check names the mortgagee, and the servicer's loss-draft department decides whether to release it in one lump sum or in staged draws tied to inspections. Each servicer has its own packet (contractor W-9, license, signed contract, lien waivers, before/after photos, inspection scheduling) and its own cadence. Contractors carry 60-120 days of working capital risk, homeowners cannot start work, and adjusters take the blame for a delay that comes after the estimate is done.
solution: A draw-management platform: it reads the carrier's payment letter and the servicer's requirements, auto-builds and submits the servicer-specific packet, schedules and preps for inspections (checklist plus timestamped photo capture), chases the servicer, and shows the contractor and homeowner a live 'money timeline.' Phase two adds a draw advance: after the servicer approves a draw schedule, the platform advances 80-90% of the next draw in days, underwritten on proprietary servicer-by-servicer release data.
why_now: Florida's AOB ban (for policies since 2023) means contractors cannot be paid directly by carriers, so they must wait on homeowners and servicers. The LA fire rebuild in 2026-27 involves thousands of large, mortgage-encumbered claims and long draw schedules. Materials costs remain volatile, which squeezes contractor cash. Regulatory rules and GSE guidelines push servicers to release funds promptly after approving a repair plan but leave the mechanics unstandardized, creating a compliance-flavored process that software can systematize.
revenue_model: Flat $295-$495 per job, or 0.5-1% of funds released. Draw advances at 2-3% of advance amount plus a 30-60 day fee, funded by a warehouse credit line. Later, per-file fees from servicers who want clean packets and fewer complaint escalations.
non_obvious_insight: The real payment terms in disaster repair are the servicer's draw curve, not the insurance company's payment speed, and nobody publishes it. Whoever logs, servicer by servicer, days-to-first-draw, inspection pass rates and packet rejection reasons owns the underwriting data for the only safe lending against insurance proceeds.
first_30_days: Sign up 5 mid-size LA fire rebuild contractors and 5 Gulf Coast roofers and offer to run their next 3 jobs through the loss-draft process as a done-for-you service at $295 per job. Log every servicer requirement in a shared spreadsheet, then turn it into a rules engine. Interview 3 former loss-draft department employees for packet-rejection patterns. Start collecting draw-timeline data, which becomes the moat and the basis for a later advance product.

title: Motor-Rewind Shops Become Drone-Motor Cells
angle: Pairing 2: Reshoring, tariffs & automation x Government / defense / municipal
one_liner: Qualify a network of existing U.S. electric-motor repair shops to wind and test compliant drone motors with non-Chinese magnets for Drone Dominance suppliers.
customer: Attritable-drone makers and tier-1 subsystem suppliers, including Gauntlet participants and Blue UAS suppliers. They pay per motor (about $60-150, my estimate, versus about $15-30 imported).
problem: The Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program targets more than 200,000 drones by 2027, and about 60,000 are to be ordered from Gauntlet 2 winners. At four motors per quadcopter that is about 240,000 motors for one tranche. China holds about 94% of magnet manufacturing, heavy rare earths stay tight through 2027, and capital is chasing airframes and software, not motors.
solution: Recruit motor-repair shops that already own winding skill, varnish and potting ovens, balancing and hipot test benches. Standardize a 'motor cell kit' (needle winders and fixtures, a single test spec, lot traceability logging) on a lease. The network operator holds customer contracts, source-verified magnet, bearing and lamination supply from domestic vendors, quality paperwork and DPAS-rated order handling, and passes work down. Each shop is audited like a franchisee.
why_now: Gauntlet cadence (roughly every six months) turns motors into a recurring bottleneck, and export controls make compliant sourcing urgent. Motor repair is a slow-shrinking industry, so shops have idle capacity. The Navy is retreating from early-stage funding, so distributed capacity without venture capital is the workable route.
revenue_model: 15-25% operator margin on motor sales, a $15-30k onboarding and equipment-lease fee per shop, and certification renewals. Later expand to ESCs, gimbals and wire harnesses using the same shop network.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is winding know-how and test discipline, not CNC capacity. Motor repair shops are typically classified as repair, so industrial-base maps built from manufacturing codes miss over a thousand of them. Hidden capacity, not new plants, is the fastest path to supply.
first_30_days: Contact regional chapters of the electrical apparatus service association to recruit 5 shops. Get 3 drone makers that currently fly Chinese motors to specify a compliant second-source design. Sell a prototype lot of about 500 motors with customer prepayment and run a first-article test.

title: IEP Chief of Staff for Special-Ed Parents
one_liner: Rich parents win school disputes with a paid educational advocate and paper trail; for $20/mo, give parents of the roughly 7.5M US students with IEPs a chief of staff who watches the legal clocks and logs every missed service minute.
customer: Parents of children with IEPs (autism, ADHD, dyslexia, speech and language delay), sold through state and local special-ed parent groups, parent training centers, pediatric practices, disability law clinics and credit unions.
problem: Districts arrive with a team; wealthy families bring an advocate ($150-400/hr) and an attorney. Federal enforcement was hollowed out (mass OSEP layoffs in October 2025, and reported moves of oversight to HHS and civil-rights enforcement to DOJ in June 2026), so parents are effectively on their own. Most violations are procedural (late evaluations, missing prior written notice, services not delivered) and go unnoticed because nobody keeps the clocks.
solution: Parent uploads the IEP and evaluations. The system builds the legal calendar (evaluation timelines from consent, meeting-notice windows, annual and triennial reviews, progress-report cadence), drafts records requests, creates a one-page pre-meeting brief (top asks plus data), and sends a same-day 'memorializing' follow-up email with prior-written-notice requests after meetings. It logs service minutes delivered vs promised, quantifying missed minutes for a compensatory-services claim, and scans the IEP for defects (no baselines, unmeasurable goals). Advocates are on-demand at $75 per 30 minutes, with a path to state complaint and due process.
why_now: The federal special-ed enforcement vacuum is documented and new as of late 2025 and mid-2026. IEP counts are rising, and LLMs can parse messy IEP PDFs and draft procedurally precise letters. Parent communities are organized on Facebook and Reddit and actively looking for help.
revenue_model: $20/mo per family; $75 advocate sessions with a revenue split to a vetted advocate co-op; $3-6 per member per month from parent centers, pediatric groups and credit unions; district-facing analytics sold only with parent consent, later.
non_obvious_insight: What the rich buy is not better argument but continuous procedural pressure: dated, written, specific requests. The subscription funds clock-watching and documentation, not advice. Parents who log service minutes turn 'I feel they're not delivering' into a quantified claim, and the paper trail is the evidence in any later dispute, so value compounds over time.
first_30_days: Publish a free IEP clock calculator and letter templates. Partner with admins of 10 state-level special-ed Facebook groups and concierge 30 families manually, measuring violations found. Convert those families to $20/mo and recruit 5 advocates for the on-demand tier.

title: Settlement Back Office for Farm Water Conservation
angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office x Water (lens: micro-farm admin and tax x agricultural water markets)
one_liner: Program administration as a service that enrolls small farms in paid fallowing and conservation programs, verifies acre-feet with satellite evapotranspiration plus meter data, pays within 14 days, and hands the farm's CPA a clean tax packet.
customer: Payers: irrigation districts, state and basin conservation programs, corporate-funded coalitions and cities buying temporary leases, who pay the admin fee. End users: family farms of 50-800 irrigated acres in the Colorado River basin.
problem: The 2027-2036 framework pushes the next cuts onto agriculture, which takes about 70% of the river. Buyers want verified acre-feet at a price per acre-foot. Farmers want simple metering and fast payment, and fear that fallowing weakens their water right. Amazon's $20M ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) shows demand with no settlement layer. Programs run on spreadsheets and site visits, so small farms wait months and mis-report the income.
solution: A portal that enrolls farms and sets a consumptive-use baseline from public field-scale ET data, pump-power meter data and the farm's own records. Local crop advisors are paid per visit to verify. Contract templates carry a 'right-protection' letter agreed with the state water agency. ACH payment in 14 days. Automatic W-9 and 1099 handling, plus a tax and books packet on income timing and conservation-payment treatment for the farm's CPA. Funders get an audit-ready acre-foot ledger.
why_now: Interior issued the Record of Decision in Aug 2026 with Powell and Mead at about 36% of capacity. 95% of the basin is in drought. Corporate and public conservation money is arriving with no back office. Free satellite ET data and cheap power-meter telemetry now make remote verification credible, and LLMs make program-specific agreements and tax packets cheap.
revenue_model: 3-5% of disbursed funds as a program admin fee. $150 per farm onboarding fee, paid by the program. Later, a spread on instant-pay float. A $100M coalition goal at 4% is about $4M of admin revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Water markets fail at settlement and trust, not price discovery. A farmer will fallow if he is paid in weeks and his water right is legally shielded. The winning product is paperwork plus a legal shield letter plus a tax packet, not a marketplace. The customer who pays is the funder who would otherwise have to staff a program office.
first_30_days: Approach 3 irrigation districts or NGOs running conservation pilots and offer to administer 20-40 farms for a flat pilot fee. Build the enrollment form, an ET baseline report from public data and ACH payout in 30 days. Sign an LOI with one coalition partner. Recruit an agricultural CPA and a water attorney as advisers to draft the shield-letter approach.

title: Philanthropic First-Loss Pool for Vet Care Loans
one_liner: Use foundation money as a loan guarantee instead of a grant, so each philanthropic dollar backs many dollars of low-APR vet credit that recycles as owners repay.
customer: Credit unions and CDFIs (lenders), private foundations (guarantee capital via program-related investments), and clinics (merchant side). End borrowers are middle-income owners who decline care.
problem: The briefing says 13% of euthanasias are attributed to inability to pay, and half of owners would be stressed by a bill of $1,000 or less. Options today are deferred-interest cards with 30%-plus APRs after the promo period, or subprime fintech loans. New philanthropy (Duffield $250M over 5 years; first grants are 250 x $10K) can't fund per-case care one grant at a time.
solution: A 'Care Guarantee Pool': a foundation funds a first-loss reserve (say 10-15% of a loan portfolio). A partner credit union or CDFI originates fixed-rate installment loans of $500-$5,000 at the clinic front desk, and the clinic is paid in about 48 hours. The vet's treatment plan is attached as collateral evidence to limit fraud, with an option to assign insurance proceeds. We run the program: clinic onboarding, application flow, servicing data and outcome reporting ('pets treated instead of euthanized').
why_now: The Duffield Foundation committed $250M on 2026-09-17, on top of PetSmart Charities' $100M pledge. Funders are looking for leverage and measurable outcomes. Embedded-lending rails (bank-as-a-service, instant payouts) make a lender-agnostic origination flow cheap to build.
revenue_model: 1-2% annual program-management fee on guaranteed balances (paid by the foundation), 2-3% origination fee from clinics, and a servicing share from the lender. Later, licensing of performance data.
non_obvious_insight: Philanthropy frames access as a subsidy problem. For the many owners who would repay an $1,800 bill over 12 months at 8% but face 30% APR or a deferred-interest trap, it is a cost-of-capital problem. A guarantee makes a one-shot grant a revolving fund, and it gives funders the proof they crave.
first_30_days: Get an LOI from one credit union or CDFI. Recruit 3 affordable-care clinics in one metro. Pitch a local community foundation and PetSmart Charities for a $250K pilot reserve (roughly $2M of loans). Use the lender's existing loan-origination software plus a simple clinic link. Model expected loss from 12-month payment-plan data at the clinics.

title: FinOps for Open-Banking Data Spend
one_liner: Bank data access is turning into a metered cost. Do for aggregator bills what cloud FinOps did for AWS bills.
customer: Fintech lenders, budgeting apps and payroll and EWA apps spending $200k-$10M per year on aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity) and direct bank APIs.
problem: The CFPB 1033 rule is stayed, and a rewrite sent to OIRA on 2026-08-06 may let banks charge aggregators past a free-request threshold (PYMNTS). Developers over-poll accounts and pay per connection and per refresh, and a fee threshold would create sudden bill shock. Nobody owns the cost line.
solution: A proxy and observability layer that dedupes and caches pulls, replaces polling with webhooks and event-based refreshes, refreshes only when a decision needs fresh data (underwriting, payday), benchmarks vendor mix and price, and forecasts spend under proposed fee scenarios.
why_now: Regulatory uncertainty is at its peak, states like New York are proposing their own regimes, and fintechs face margin pressure. Any fee threshold in the rewrite turns data access into variable cost of goods sold.
revenue_model: 15-20% of verified savings (gainshare) or $2k-$10k per month SaaS.
non_obvious_insight: Data-access cost is becoming a real COGS line that finance teams can't yet see. My hypothesis is that dedupe and smarter refresh timing alone save 20-40%, so the first step is an audit that verifies it. A fee threshold makes that savings pool bigger.
first_30_days: Offer a free aggregator bill audit to 20 fintechs (they share invoices and usage exports). Quantify wasteful pulls, convert two to a 15% gainshare agreement, and publish the anonymized benchmark.

title: Audit Desk for Indie Labels' AI-Remix Royalties
one_liner: Independent monitoring, consent management and statement auditing for the royalties that AI covers and remixes will start generating.
customer: Indie labels and publishers with 500-50,000 tracks, including Merlin, A2IM and IMPALA members, and their managers. Later, Merlin itself or collecting societies.
problem: Spotify and UMG will sell fan AI covers and remixes as a paid Premium add-on with 'consent, credit, compensation,' but no attribution method has been disclosed. Merlin joined on Aug 4, and Deezer's remix feature needs artist consent (Jun 24). Indie rights-holders will soon receive statement lines for derivative uses they cannot verify, across several programs with different opt-in rules.
solution: A dashboard that normalizes consent and pricing terms across programs (Spotify, Deezer, YouTube, licensed generators). An independent detector samples public remix and cover outputs using stem-level audio similarity to estimate each catalog's derivative usage. It reconciles the estimate against reported statements and prepares audit-rights letters when the numbers do not match. Delivered as a monthly report plus software.
why_now: The first major licensed-derivative programs launched in 2026, and Suno's Sep 9 move to a licensed-trained model shows a pay-for-use market forming. Indies have the least data and the weakest audit position.
revenue_model: $500-2,000/month per label, plus a contingency of 10-15% on recovered underpayments, which is standard for royalty audits, and an enterprise deal with an indie body.
non_obvious_insight: When a new royalty stream launches without a disclosed attribution method, the party with the least data needs an independent auditor. Royalty auditing is an established, profitable profession that no one has built for AI derivatives yet.
first_30_days: Take 10 indie labels through Merlin and A2IM contacts. Produce a free 'Derivative Exposure Report' scanning YouTube, TikTok and Deezer previews for AI covers of each label's top 50 tracks. Sell the monthly monitor, and recruit an advisor from a royalty-audit firm.

title: Unfreeze Desk for Indian UPI Merchants
one_liner: A court-ready dossier generator and fixed-fee advocate network that unfreezes shopkeepers' bank accounts after a scam victim's UPI money passes through them, with a freeze-continuity layer later.
customer: Small merchants, traders, fuel-station owners and freelancers in India whose current or savings accounts get frozen because a scam victim's money passed through their UPI QR. They pay per case (₹3,000-8,000) or a ₹199/month subscription. Chartered accountants and trader associations are the referral channel.
problem: Automated cyber-fraud freezes catch innocent recipients. One Faridabad scam of ₹4.43 crore led to more than 36,000 frozen accounts, mostly small merchants. A Mumbai shop owner was frozen over ₹826 and spent over a month trying to get access back. A retailer's ₹8.26 lakh current account was blocked over a single ₹1,000 UPI payment. Relief takes months, and working capital, payroll and supplier payments stall.
solution: Merchants upload the bank statement and freeze notice, and software extracts the flagged credit, payer VPA, invoices and merchant-vintage evidence. It then produces a bundle for the bank nodal officer and police investigating officer, and a draft writ petition citing the Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Rajasthan High Court rulings that a merchant cannot verify each UPI payer. Partner advocates file and appear at a fixed fee, and the tool tracks the case. Phase 2: a 'clean receipts' setup (order-ID dynamic QR, invoice per payment, a separate working-capital account) and an NBFC-funded bridge advance against the frozen balance.
why_now: The Andhra Pradesh High Court ruled in July 2026 that authorities cannot freeze a merchant's whole account for receiving a UPI payment from an accused, and other High Courts have said the same. That gives a template-able legal remedy where before it was ad hoc. The Faridabad freezes and the Home Ministry review put the problem in the news. UPI acceptance among tiny merchants keeps growing.
revenue_model: Fixed case fee of ₹3,000-8,000 (unfreeze package plus advocate), a ₹199/month 'Merchant Shield' subscription that keeps an evidence dossier updated, and referral fees from NBFC partners for frozen-balance bridge loans. Later B2B licensing to UPI QR aggregators and bank merchant-onboarding teams.
non_obvious_insight: The merchant is not defrauded. The loss is working capital held hostage by a blunt automated tool that recovers almost nothing, so banks over-freeze. A Parliamentary Standing Committee found only ₹0.57 crore recovered out of ₹2,294.79 crore lost to cyber fraud in 2022, about 0.02%. So the freeze is structural false-positive management, not an anti-fraud problem, and the buyer is desperate on day one. Police in Faridabad said 'People come crying. Some had only ₹200 or ₹500 transferred to their accounts, yet the banks froze them.' Evidence: https://the420.in/faridabad-cyber-scam-upi-fraud-accounts-frozen-home-ministry/ and https://www.medianama.com/2026/07/223-merchants-bank-accounts-frozen-upi-payments-fraudsters-andhra-hc/.
first_30_days: Days 1-5: Build a WhatsApp intake bot and landing page in Hindi and English ('Account freeze ho gaya? 10 minute mein case file'). Sign 3 partner advocates in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Hyderabad at a fixed split. Days 5-15: Template the dossier and petition from the three High Court rulings and have the advocates review it. Post explainer videos in Hindi and Gujarati on YouTube and Reels, and in trader WhatsApp and Telegram groups where frozen merchants already vent. Days 15-30: Close the first 20-30 paid cases, publish anonymized turnaround times, and approach two CA firms and one trader association for referrals. The design must keep filings with licensed advocates to avoid unauthorized-practice issues.

title: Audit-Grade Inventory Robots for Defense Property
angle: Pairing 2: Logistics & physical automation x Government/defense/municipal
one_liner: Drone and rover inventory counts that produce tamper-evident audit evidence, sold first to defense contractors who must physically inventory government-furnished property, then to Pentagon depots racing a clean-audit deadline.
customer: Property managers at small and mid-size defense contractors (machine shops, depot-level repair firms, integrators holding government property). Later, DoD depots and audit-readiness contractors that need count observation.
problem: DoD has never passed a full financial audit and has set a clean-opinion goal of about 2028 (verify), and inventory and materiel existence are among the biggest obstacles. Leaders admit they lack supply-chain data to support a '90-, 120-, 180-day fight'. Federal staff capacity is shrinking (OPM rating caps, contested reorganizations) and agencies keep buying capacity. Contractors holding government property (FAR 52.245-1) must keep records and do periodic physical inventories that DCMA property administrators review, and the work is manual and labor-heavy.
solution: Deploy indoor drones, rovers and wearable scanners to produce time-stamped, geotagged, hash-chained count evidence reconciled to property records. Output exception lists in the format auditors and property administrators expect. Use offline-first, air-gapped operation, since air-gap-native tooling (Defense Unicorns) cut authorization from 18 months to about 2 weeks. Begin in low-hazard bays and add ordnance-safe hardware later.
why_now: Warehouse inventory drones matured in commercial logistics but were never packaged for federal audit evidence. The Pentagon's comfort with small drones jumped through Drone Dominance, and audit-readiness spending is a live budget line. Federal staffing cuts push work to contractors.
revenue_model: Per verified location or per count event, priced below manual count crews, with annual recurring programs for contractors. Later, per-depot audit-evidence programs through subcontracts.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not logistics but the CFO and audit-readiness office, which has a statutory deadline and money, while logistics chiefs have no robot budget. Selling robots as 'audit evidence' unlocks the funding. Contractor-held government property is a commercial beachhead with a private budget.
first_30_days: Recruit two defense contractors with large government-property holdings and one small audit or property-compliance firm. Do a free count at one facility to define the evidence format. Then price a paid annual inventory at each and pursue a small DLA or Army innovation solicitation.

title: Hatchery-Specific Phage Cocktails on Subscription
one_liner: A monthly service that isolates each shrimp hatchery's own Vibrio strains and ships a custom bacteriophage cocktail to kill them, so hatcheries can stop using antibiotics.
customer: Shrimp hatcheries and nurseries in Vietnam, India, Ecuador and Indonesia, plus the exporters and feed companies that buy their post-larvae and need antibiotic-free supply.
problem: Vibrio outbreaks (AHPND/EMS) wipe out whole hatchery batches. Antibiotics are banned in export markets, but residues keep turning up: a 2025 analysis attributes 43% of shrimp export rejections by the EU, US and Japan to chloramphenicol and nitrofuran residues, and 19 Indian consignments were rejected in 2025-26. Post-larvae pass through fragmented hatcheries and aggregators, so nobody can trace or fix the source. Generic probiotics and disinfectants work unevenly.
solution: A lab-in-a-box subscription. We sample water and biofilm each month and sequence and culture the local Vibrio isolates. We screen them against a curated phage library and ship a hatchery-specific cocktail as a water or feed additive. The cocktail is refreshed as strains drift, and later we add AI-designed phages. Each shipment comes with a residue-free 'clean seed' data pack that exporters and buyers can audit. Selling it in the feed-additive or probiotic regulatory class, not as a drug, keeps approval fast in most shrimp-producing countries.
why_now: Antibiotic bans (India's March 2025 notification banning chloramphenicol and nitrofurans in food-producing animals) are colliding with continued export rejections. Generative phage design became real in September 2025, when the Arc Institute and Stanford, using the Evo genome models, produced 16 viable AI-designed phage genomes from 302 candidates, later published in Science. Nanopore sequencing is cheap enough to run near ponds. Buyers now demand antibiotic-free attestations.
revenue_model: Subscription of roughly $400-1,500 per month per hatchery, scaled by tank volume, plus per-batch emergency cocktails at a premium. Exporters or feed companies pay a per-lot attestation fee. Longer term, license the phage library and drift dataset to feed and biosecurity companies.
non_obvious_insight: A phage is host-specific and keeps evolving with its target, so it works badly as a mass-market molecule and well as a perishable, local, continuously updated service. Big pharma cannot profitably do bespoke, and that is the wedge. The moat is the living library of regional strains and the resistance-drift dataset, and the hatchery is the chokepoint of the whole seed supply chain, so clean seed pays off downstream.
first_30_days: Partner with one university phage lab in Vietnam, India or Ecuador. Offer 10 hatcheries free strain-isolation reports to build the initial library, and pitch each hatchery a $500-per-month paid pilot. Ask one export processor to sponsor 3 pilots to secure antibiotic-free seed for its supply chain.

title: Signed-Capture Verified UGC for DTC Ads
one_liner: A capture SDK and verification API that proves a testimonial video came from a real, purchasing customer, for brands exposed to the FTC's fake-review rules.
customer: DTC and e-commerce brands spending on paid social, UGC agencies and marketplaces, and performance-marketing agencies with legal exposure.
problem: The FTC's rule on fake reviews and testimonials (effective Oct 2024) covers AI-generated testimonials from people who do not exist, with civil penalties above $50k per violation. AI 'UGC ad' generators now produce fake customers, and creators can deliver them through marketplaces without the brand knowing. Brands want real customers for conversion and cannot tell the difference.
solution: A web and native capture flow that records a testimonial with device attestation (Apple App Attest, Play Integrity), a random liveness phrase and a signed C2PA manifest, linked to a verified purchase through a Shopify order token. It outputs a 'Verified Real Customer' badge and an evidence file per ad. A batch API scans videos delivered through other tools, attests what can be attested and flags what cannot.
why_now: The FTC rule is in force, platforms are labeling AI content, and avatar-UGC volume has exploded. Provenance signals in phones and the C2PA ecosystem make signed capture cheap.
revenue_model: $3-8 per verified video, $500-3k/month agency plans, and a Shopify app subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The authenticity premium is really a compliance premium. Liability sits with the brand rather than the avatar vendor, so a legal-risk budget pays for it, not a marketing budget.
first_30_days: Ship a web capture flow linked to Shopify order tokens before any native SDK. Recruit 10 DTC brands through Shopify communities and UGC agencies at $5 per video, and run one campaign comparing verified and unverified creatives.

title: Swimmer-Distress Drones for Endurance Events
one_liner: A race-day service using thermal-camera drones and AI to spot swimmers in trouble before rescue boats do.
customer: Triathlon, open-water swim and Ironman-style race directors, event insurers, and municipalities running beach swims.
problem: Most triathlon deaths occur in the swim, and safety still depends on kayaks and volunteers scanning choppy water. A study at the 2018 IRONMAN Mont-Tremblant found drones identified 1 of 5 distress events before rescue boats saw them, and human spotters tire.
solution: An operator-plus-software service: one or two drones with visible and thermal cameras track the swim course, AI flags prolonged stillness, vertical posture or flailing, and alerts go to the rescue coordinator by radio app, with a post-race report for insurers. Later add wearable tags and AED delivery.
why_now: Thermal drone cameras and edge vision models are cheap, FAA rules for wider drone operations are advancing, and open-water race participation is climbing.
revenue_model: $2.5-8k per event, annual series contracts, and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: The pain sits with event insurers and small race directors, for whom one fatality can end the event, so the pitch is loss reduction with data. AI is valuable mainly because it does not get tired.
first_30_days: Buy two drones (about $8k), recruit a licensed Part 107 pilot and a lifeguard consultant, provide free coverage at two local swims to collect labeled footage, and pitch 10 small triathlon directors a $1.5k pilot.

title: Distressed Recycling Equipment Exchange
one_liner: A broker-refurbisher that moves equipment from failed US recycling plants to funded buyers abroad, with commissioning included.
customer: Recyclers in India, Mexico, Turkey, Southeast Asia and Africa building capacity (buyers), sourcing from receivers, lenders and former owners.
problem: More than a quarter of US PET recycling capacity closed in 12 months (7 of about 30). Ascend Elements filed Chapter 11 in April 2026, Li-Cycle went bankrupt in 2025, and Solarcycle paused a plant. Washing lines, extruders, optical sorters and reactors are stranded, while India earmarked about $166M to subsidize recycling capacity.
solution: Catalog equipment with photos and condition reports, bundle it into 'line packages', refurbish and test, ship, and send a commissioning team. Give buyers financing-ready documentation and give receivers a fast, credible exit.
why_now: 2025-26 produced an unusual wave of high-spec recycling plant failures, and subsidy money abroad creates buyers, both at once.
revenue_model: 10-20% commission on sales plus refurbishment and commissioning fees.
non_obvious_insight: General industrial liquidators do not know which line is a working PET wash line. Domain knowledge plus buyer matching is the margin, and it grows every time another recycler fails.
first_30_days: Contact the receivers and lenders for the 7 closed reclaimers and other failed plants. Build an equipment inventory with photos. Pre-sell to 5 Indian or Mexican buyers before taking on any inventory.
